correctness.rationale: For the specified 13 rational points, normalization gives the projective plane; a four-arc defines a quadrangle whose pencil over F3 has the three line-pair quadrics and one smooth member. Counting unions is by distinct Boolean memberships, not by conic pairs. A separate exact reconstruction reproduced 234 arcs, 4,641 concepts and the whole face vector (1,13,78,286,715,1287,1716,1638) over 8,192 supports, including exactly the 78 two-line forbidden seven-sets. In the online recursion, all feasible first queries are considered; each costs one level and thereafter the shorter child depth is binding. Empty branches cannot support a root query and a repeated query cannot split. Exact backward evaluation of 1,594,323 states (1,520,013 nonempty) gives depth 8, excluding 9. The supplied tree was checked as data: 511 nodes, 256 distinct branches of depth 8 with matching nonzero leaf counts and no repeated path query. Replay and output: /workspace/branches/548ce169-3110-49e6-8a32-35f468de46b1/independent_verify.py and independent_check.json. Neither supplied script was executed. For the structural claim, two forbidden sevens share at most five points; basis exchange follows since at most one replacement can be forbidden and the sole-candidate case is the other base. Each six-set extends to a base. Each forbidden seven is a circuit and its extension by any outside point has rank seven, hence it is a hyperplane. Complements of forbidden sevens meet pairwise in at most four points, so dual bases similarly give paving, proving sparse paving. Shellability of the pure six-dimensional independence complex gives the integral sphere wedge, with multiplicity 714 from reduced Euler characteristic; independent binary boundary rank 924 corroborates but does not prove the integral statement. The decisive static and adaptive conclusions use full support/state enumeration, not the auxiliary orbit table.
